memory_update.text: PI should remain a priority underfollowed candidate for the retail shrink and inventory-accuracy node because it supplies core RAIN RFID item-level infrastructure and sits one layer upstream from retailers.

RSKD is a small-cap speculative software candidate for the digital side of shrink: ecommerce fraud, chargebacks, account abuse, return abuse, and policy abuse. Survival in later layers requires proof of enterprise retail spend growth and durable unit economics.
ZBRA and AVY form useful reference anchors for RFID-enabled inventory accuracy and retail loss-prevention infrastructure, but their size and diversification reduce hidden-alpha purity.

Need a later pass on private or non-US-listed leaders in EAS, smart cases/locks, computer-vision shrink prevention, and retail security services because several direct operators in this node may not be US-listed pure plays.
PI is the cleanest underfollowed public-market mapping for RAIN RFID infrastructure tied to retail inventory accuracy and omnichannel reliability.

VYX should be tracked as a checkout-layer shrink/fraud-control supplier; key uncertainty is whether self-checkout shrink backlash hurts hardware demand or increases demand for analytics and fraud controls.
DMRC is a below-$300M speculative exception with explicit retail loss-prevention language but needs hard evidence of material retailer deployments and ARR conversion.
The node decomposes into four investable supplier layers: RFID chips/readers, RFID labels/inlays, checkout/POS fraud analytics, and digital identity/watermarking for product or gift-card fraud.
Need later-layer verification of customer concentration, named retailer deployments, retail revenue materiality, and whether shrink-prevention budgets are expanding despite retailer capex discipline.

PI should be tracked as the highest-relevance underfollowed public-market candidate for the retail RFID and item-level inventory-accuracy node; verify retail adoption breadth beyond apparel and footwear.

RSKD opens a digital-shrink sub-lane: ecommerce fraud, chargebacks, returns abuse, refund claims, and policy-abuse analytics are adjacent to physical shrink but may have different unit economics and risk profiles.
NSSC is a speculative second-order store-security candidate; retail exposure exists in product/vertical language but materiality must be proven before it survives later Serenity layers.
The node splits into at least three investable sub-lanes: item-level RFID/inventory accuracy, digital fraud/returns-abuse software, and physical store hardening/access-control infrastructure.

Many pure-play retail loss-prevention assets are private or embedded inside larger companies, including Sensormatic inside Johnson Controls and Checkpoint Systems inside CCL Industries; public-market mapping therefore requires supplier and component-level screens.
Impinj should be retained for Layer 2 verification as a relatively pure RAIN RFID endpoint IC/platform beneficiary of item-level retail inventory accuracy, shrink visibility, and authentication.
Riskified is a small-cap speculative discovery candidate for the digital-shrink lane: ecommerce fraud, returns abuse, chargebacks, and policy abuse.

Avery Dennison is not usually framed as a shrink-prevention company, but its RFID intelligent-label and source-tagging role creates a plausible second-order exposure to retail inventory accuracy and omnichannel execution.

Sensormatic Solutions under Johnson Controls appears highly relevant to EAS, RFID, inventory intelligence, and loss-prevention analytics, but JCI is diversified; consider a separate reference-context pass or look for smaller public suppliers around Sensormatic-compatible tags, cases, sensors, and installation services.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded a focused two-lane universe for public companies directly exposed to retail shrink, RFID-enabled inventory accuracy, and ecommerce fraud prevention. The strongest underfollowed candidate is Impinj because it is a relatively pure RAIN RFID infrastructure provider used for item-level visibility. Riskified is a smaller speculative software candidate tied to ecommerce fraud and policy-abuse control. Zebra and Avery Dennison are reference leaders with direct RFID, retail operations, labeling, and loss-prevention relevance, but their larger and more diversified profiles make them better context anchors than hidden alpha candidates. Expanded the node around scarce retail shrink and inventory-accuracy infrastructure. The most relevant US-listed candidates are not retailers themselves but RFID chip/platform vendors, item-level label/inlay suppliers, POS/self-checkout software vendors, and niche digital-watermark/fraud-prevention providers. Reference context includes large incumbents such as Johnson Controls' Sensormatic and Avery Dennison; the underfollowed lane is stronger in Impinj, NCR Voyix, and speculative micro-cap Digimarc. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the universe around retail shrink, RFID inventory accuracy, ecommerce fraud, access control, and store-security infrastructure.
